issues.feedback: The spec changes `BackendRegistry::get_or_create_for_spec` to require a role, but only lists orchestrator callsites. You also need a plan for `src/cli/prd.rs`, `src/cli/quick_prd.rs`, `src/cli/auto.rs`, `src/mcp/handlers.rs`, and preload helpers, or provide a backward-compatible overload.

Current parse-retry logic uses `registry.get(&reformatter_spec)` and executes with the original role label. With role-keyed caching, this likely misses and falls back to the original backend/timeout, so `reformatter` timeout may never apply. The spec should require explicit reformatter-role backend acquisition (e.g., create/get with role `reformatter`).

You add `acceptance_qa` timeout fields but orchestrator acceptance QA currently executes as role `qa`. The spec must explicitly decide whether acceptance QA uses `qa` timeout or `acceptance_qa`, then update callsites/tests consistently.

Deprecating `backends.*.timeout_seconds` only in `GlobalConfig::load` is incomplete. `ralph config set backends.*.timeout_seconds` will still appear to work while being ignored. Define explicit behavior (reject or warn on set/get), and define precedence when both deprecated and new configs are present.

If you add new timeout config (especially project overrides), the spec also needs updates for `config show/get` effective views (`src/cli/config.rs`) and MCP config-show payloads so users can read effective timeout values. Otherwise feature visibility is inconsistent.

The test plan omits required validate conformance updates. Existing conformance tests currently depend on `backends.*.timeout_seconds` (`tests_streaming`, `tests_e2e_conformance`) and will need migration, plus new validate coverage for role-specific timeout behavior and deprecation handling.

Requirements ask for workspace-configurable role timeouts, but the spec adds project-level timeout overrides. This is scope expansion; either justify and add acceptance criteria for it, or remove it to reduce risk and keep implementation focused.
